newsitem.title: USA: Dow snaps losing streak, aided by solid 3M results.
newsitem.headline: Dow snaps losing streak, aided by solid 3M results.

text.p: U.S. blue chips snapped their four-session losing streak and were restored to an above 6000 close, bolstered by an unexpectedly strong quarterly earnings report from Dow component Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing.

"Investors are taking a stand at the 6000 mark and there's a normal adjustment to the selloff of recent sessions," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research. He also noted buying related to "good earnings by 3M."
The Dow industrials rose 14 to about 6007, after ending below 6000 on Thursday for the first time in two weeks.
For the week, the blue chip index slid 87 points.
The Nasdaq Composite slipped four on Friday to about 1223.
Losers and gainers were about even on moderate NYSE volume of about 365 million shares.

Stocks were pressured at the open after bonds sold off on news that September U.S. durable goods rose a much stronger-than-expected 4.6 percent, the biggest jump since December 1992. But bonds later cut losses as a closer look showed most of the orders gain came from the volatile civilian aircraft component. August's drop was revised downward.
The long bond was up 15/32 to yield 6.81 percent.

3M surged 3-1/8 to 74-3/8, aiding the Dow by about nine points. The stock touched a 52-week high of 74-1/2 after reporting third-quarter operating earnings rose to $0.95 a share from $0.81 a share a year ago. The September quarter was 3M's first since spinning off Imation Corp, its data storage and imaging businesses which had restrained 3M's results.

Friday's overall activity slowed as Wall Street braced for the upcoming slew of economic reports. Reports set for release next week include third-quarter Employment Cost Index, October consumer confidence, third-quarter preliminary gross domestic product, and Friday's key October jobs report.

"The market is still in a short-term corrective cycle. There's limited upside surprise potential and more likely vulnerability to downward side potential unless we have new evidence that inflation is under control," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott.
Peggy Farley, chief executive of Amas Securities, agreed that the market was in a holding pattern on Friday ahead of a full economic calendar next week.
But she added that, "Several IPOs were reasonably well-received which is always good. That's a bullish sign for the market overall."
Among those making their Wall Street debuts, Triumph Group, an aircraft component maker, rose 2-3/4 to 21-3/4, and Metris Cos, a direct marketer of consumer products, surged 4-3/8 to 20-3/8.
P.J. America, which operates 42 Papa John's pizza stores, jumped 3-7/8 to 16-3/8 in its first day of trading. Another IPO, Stage Stores, which operates clothing stores, rallied 2-3/4 to 19-1/4.
Among individual shares, Chubb climbed 5-3/8 to 50-7/8 after telling analysts in a conference call it was mulling the possible sale of its life and real estate businesses.

Some drug stocks were weaker after recent strength. Bristol Myers lost 2-3/4 to 105-3/4, Schering-Plough was off 2-1/4 to 64-1/4, Eli Lilly fell two to 69-3/4 and Dow component Merck shed 1-3/4 to 73-3/8.

Aetna rose three to 63-1/8 after defying uncertainty elsewhere in the HMO industry by meeting analysts' expectations for third-quarter earnings. Its results included the newly acquired U.S. Healthcare.
ETEC Systems tumbled 12-7/8 points or 36 percent to 23-1/8 after warning of a first-quarter shortfall.

Stocks hammered after quarterly earnings reports included Shared Medical, off 6-1/4 to 49-1/2, Inter-Tel, off 7-3/4 to 13-7/8. Gateway 2000 lost 4-7/8 to 50-1/4 after topping the Street consensus but warned of rising expenses. Octel lost 8-3/4 to 15-3/4 after reporting in-line results and disclosing a delay in the release of a software upgrade.
RadiSys rallied 6-7/8 to 68 after reporting a jump in quarterly results. Likewise, American Power Conversion surged 3-5/8 to 19-7/8.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 4.40 to 1222.60.
The S&P 500 index fell 1.37 to 700.92.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
